label: L=9 sequences, second copy step (t=10, outputting orig(1))
explanation: Very sparse, weak unit (max 0.007). It fires only in the copy phase of length-9 sequences: about 90% of activations and mass are at t=10 (recall_idx 1, input is orig(0) fed back after <DEL>, output is orig(1)), and the rest are at t=11 (recall_idx 2). It never fires in the original or delimiter phases or for L<8. Even inside that slot it fires on only about 2% of sequences, so precision is very low. Which sequences fire depends on the tokens: a first token of j, u or i (lift 4-7x) and a second token of u, j or b. Restricting to first token in {j,u,i} raises precision to 11% but costs half the recall, and adding second-token sets reaches F1 about 0.28, which looks overfit. The largest activations come from sequences that start u j or j i.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=j (+2.94), phase=2 & in_tok=u (+2.93), phase=2 & in_tok=i (+2.31), prev_tok=n (+2.13), t=10 & prev_tok=<DEL> (+2.00), L=9 & recall_idx=1 (+2.00). Lower it: orig8=- (-2.22), orig2=r (-1.75), orig3=v (-1.43).
